title: Batch Normalization & Dropout 🧪
description: Stabilize and regularize deep CNNs with BatchNorm and Dropout.

slides.title: The Internal Covariate Shift ⚖️
slides.content:
# Why BatchNorm?

As weights update, the distribution of each layer's inputs changes. This slows training. **Batch Normalization** normalizes the activations of each mini‑batch:

$$\hat{x} = \frac{x - \mu_{batch}}{\sqrt{\sigma^2_{batch} + \epsilon}}$$

Then scales and shifts with learnable parameters γ, β.

Benefits:
* Allows higher learning rates.
* Reduces sensitivity to initialization.
* Acts as a slight regularizer.

slides.title: Dropout for Regularization 🎲
slides.content:
## Randomly Zero Neurons

`nn.Dropout(p)` randomly zeroes a fraction `p` of the inputs during **training only**.

It prevents co‑adaptation of neurons, forcing them to learn robust features independently.

Typical values: `p=0.2` to `0.5`. Often used before final classifier layers.

slides.title: Dropout in a CNN
slides.content: Apply dropout after the feature extractor.
slides.codeSnippet:
features = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.MaxPool2d(2),
    nn.Dropout2d(p=0.25)   # dropout on feature maps
)
classifier = nn.Linear(64 * 8 * 8, 10)  # after pooling, if input was 32

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Order of Operations: Conv → BN → ReLU

This order is most common and effective. `nn.Sequential(conv, bn, relu)`.
